section_summary: This section examines Japan’s gold, foreign exchange, securities, silver, and access to foreign credit in 1939. It also contains correspondence about Japanese government bonds, proposed Swiss credit, American loans connected to Japan’s electric power industry, and British credit facilities. Several cross-reference notes point to related records filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of memoranda on Japanese resources and an embargo
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department sends two confidential memoranda for Embassy comment.
subfiles.summary: Transmits studies on Japanese resources and an import and export embargo, restricting them to staff use because some data came from confidential sources.

subfiles.title: Japanese Gold and Foreign Exchange Resources, Part I
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Estimates Japan’s internationally realizable assets and their rate of depletion.
subfiles.summary: Estimates assets fell from $789 million at the end of 1936 to $487 million at the end of 1938. At the 1938 rate of depletion, they might last about four more years, though future trade deficits are uncertain. An April 1939 estimate places gold reserves at $215 million.

subfiles.title: Japanese Gold and Foreign Exchange Resources, Part II: Supporting Data
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Documents the evidence and assumptions behind estimates of Japan’s gold and other external assets.
subfiles.summary: Reconciles State Department and Federal Reserve estimates of gold reserves at approximately $229 million at the end of February 1939. It assesses mobilizable foreign securities, Japanese external bonds, silver, bank exchange balances, and the deficit in Japan’s non-yen-bloc current account. Appendices detail estimated old-gold purchases and monthly gold-stock calculations through April 1939.

subfiles.title: Handwritten comment on Haan’s electric power loan letter
subfiles.about: Comments on claims concerning foreign shareholders and Japanese electric power loans.
subfiles.summary: Questions Haan’s account of shareholders’ rights and the relevance of Oriental Development Company loans to Japan’s credit position.

subfiles.title: Sino-Korean Peoples League letter on American loans and Japanese power companies
subfiles.about: Urges the United States to prevent American credit from supporting Japanese expansion.
subfiles.summary: Haan alleges that American loans to Japanese electric power companies are being transferred to a nationalized company with government backing. He links Japanese bank financing to operations in Manchuria and opium cultivation, and asks Hull to curb Japanese access to American credit.

subfiles.title: Statement on Japanese government invitations to foreigners
subfiles.about: Lists foreign visitors invited to Japan and questions whether they will spread Japanese propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Describes planned visits by American businesspeople, financiers, educators, journalists, and other foreign guests, with concern that they will return with favorable Japanese publicity.

subfiles.title: Siegelstein letter concerning the Hovey estate’s Japanese bonds
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Green H. Hackworth
subfiles.about: Seeks diplomatic presentation of the Hovey estate’s bond claim while separate court proceedings continue.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein says discovery proceedings against Yokohama Specie Bank do not displace the estate’s claim against Japan. He asks the Department to raise the claim with Japanese diplomatic representatives.

subfiles.title: Department reply on the Hovey estate’s bond claim
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Declines to espouse the Hovey claim without proof of legal entitlement to the bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department says the claimant’s right to replacement bonds must first be established through the pending court case or other appropriate legal proceedings.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on the National Mobilization Law
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on enforcement of Japanese price regulations.
subfiles.summary: References despatch 3778 on price controls and a proposed Price Bureau.

subfiles.title: Division note on British credits to Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Embassy’s report that British credit lines to Japanese interests continue to shrink.
subfiles.summary: British credits and Japanese paper in London are declining toward a minimum sustained by longstanding business ties.

subfiles.title: British Credits to Japan
subfiles.from: Herschel V. Johnson, for the Ambassador
subfiles.about: Updates the Department on British banking and commercial credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports a continuing gradual reduction in credit lines and little Japanese paper in the London discount market. Further contraction could follow if Japan’s policy becomes openly hostile to Great Britain.

subfiles.title: Bern telegram on proposed Swiss machinery credit
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed Swiss credit for machinery exports to Japan or Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: After an unsuccessful Japanese loan approach, a firm sought 50 million Swiss francs in bank credit backed by Swiss export-risk guarantees. Some Swiss officials and the national bank oppose the guarantee.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Bern telegram on Swiss credit
subfiles.about: Restates the Bern report about Swiss financing of machinery exports.
subfiles.summary: Records the proposed bank credit, requested government guarantee, and opposition within Swiss official circles.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Bern on credits to Japanese agents
subfiles.about: Directs the Legation to convey the Department’s views on Japanese credits to Swiss authorities.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes confidential oral discussion of American credit policy and notes similar British practice.

subfiles.title: Edgerton letter opposing credit to Japan
subfiles.about: Opposes extending American credit to Japan for cotton and oil.
subfiles.summary: Edgerton objects to a reported Japanese credit proposal and praises Hull’s conduct of foreign affairs.

subfiles.title: Hamilton reply to Edgerton
subfiles.about: Responds to Edgerton’s concern about American credit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: States that the government has extended no credit and knows of no substantial private credits to Japan.

subfiles.title: Division note on Japan Advertiser annual review
subfiles.about: Calls attention to the Embassy’s covering despatch for an annual economic review.
subfiles.summary: Notes receipt of the Japan Advertiser review and recommends reading the despatch’s second paragraph.

subfiles.title: Japan Advertiser Annual Review, 1938–1939
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japan Advertiser’s annual review of Japanese finance, industry, and commerce.
subfiles.summary: Highlights Charles Nelson Spinks’s assessment of Japan’s wartime economy, charts of industrial production and trade, and a compilation of government bond sales.

subfiles.title: Siegelstein letter challenging refusal of the Hovey claim
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Green H. Hackworth
subfiles.about: Objects to delaying diplomatic action on the Hovey estate’s claim.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein argues that court proceedings against the fiscal agent and a diplomatic claim against Japan can proceed concurrently. He fears delay and asks how the Department would respond if the court lacks jurisdiction.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Siegelstein’s July letter
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Again declines to submit the Hovey claim without evidence of its legal validity.
subfiles.summary: Says the claimant’s right to the bonds must be judicially established before the Department can reconsider diplomatic presentation.

subfiles.title: Steinberg inquiry about Tokyo Electric bonds
subfiles.to: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Asks whether to keep or sell Tokyo Electric bonds amid conditions in the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Steinberg says selling would cost about half his capital and requests advice.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Steinberg
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Declines to advise Steinberg whether to hold or sell Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Suggests that Steinberg consult a reliable local banking institution.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on economic pressure against Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum of conversation with the French ambassador.
subfiles.summary: References French views on using economic and financial pressure against Japan.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Manchurian industrial credit
subfiles.about: Points to a conversation with Henry Breck about credit to a Manchurian corporation.
subfiles.summary: References discussion of credits to the Manchurian Industrial Development Corporation.

subfiles.title: Siegelstein letter renewing the Hovey estate claim
subfiles.about: Again asks for the Hovey claim to be presented to Japanese representatives.
subfiles.summary: Siegelstein argues that Japan cannot be sued in New York and that proceedings against Yokohama Specie Bank face jurisdictional objections. He insists the verified petition is sufficient for diplomatic presentation.

subfiles.title: Department reply to Siegelstein’s August letter
subfiles.about: Refers Siegelstein to prior explanations of the Department’s position.
subfiles.summary: Directs Siegelstein to the Department’s July 17 letter concerning proof of entitlement to the bonds.

subfiles.title: Division note on further decline in London credit facilities
subfiles.about: Summarizes London’s latest despatch on Japanese credit facilities.
subfiles.summary: Reports reliable indications of a further decline despite the absence of precise figures.

subfiles.title: British Credits to Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits a British parliamentary exchange about Japanese credit facilities in London.
subfiles.summary: The despatch begins by referring to earlier Embassy reports and enclosing an excerpt from Hansard; it continues beyond this section.
